title: UK retains early access to test latest US AI models
key_facts: Britain will retain early access to the latest AI models for safety testing, the AI minister confirmed on Monday (12 Oct 2026), after reports that the White House had restricted the UK's access.

Kanishka Narayan, the UK AI minister, said in a London speech that the government has been working with the US government to keep access for Britain's AI Security Institute to the most powerful models before release.
AFP calls it a reversal of the Trump administration's earlier request that OpenAI and Anthropic not share models with the UK lab before US assessment, according to several media outlets.
Narayan said the institute has been given access to Google's most powerful model, Gemini 4 Argon, which AFP says has not been released publicly over safety concerns.
Narayan warned it "seems likely, if not inevitable, that our own cyber defences will be breached".
He urged AI labs to "listen when your scientists warn of severe dangers" and, if they cannot control the risks, not to release the system.
Government pilot schemes use frontier AI to find and fix vulnerabilities in public services.
Microsoft president Brad Smith told the BBC the UK is best placed to lead on AI testing and that milk and washing machines are more heavily regulated than AI.
quote_evidence: "We have been working closely with the US government... to retain access for Britain's AI Security Institute to the most powerful AI models before they are released," AI minister Kanishka Narayan said in a speech in London.

Narayan said Britain's AI Security Institute, established in 2023, had been granted access to Google's most powerful AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, which has not been released publicly over safety concerns.
Narayan on Monday warned that "it seems likely, if not inevitable, that our own cyber defences will be breached".
why_it_matters_hint: The UK government says its AI safety institute will keep testing the most powerful US models before release, after reports that the US had tried to limit that access.
notes: AFP's text says Gemini 4 Argon had not been released publicly; The Verge reported on 13 Oct 2026 that Google then launched it to Pro and Ultra subscribers, so the 'not public' statement describes the position at the time of the speech. The pool dates the AFP page 13 Oct, Japan Today carried it on 12 Oct (evening), so the event is a day older than the window.
